citation: Worth, J., Sizmur, J., Walker, M., Bradshaw, S., & Styles, B. (2017). Teacher Observation: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluation by the National Foundation for Educational Research [NFER]; intervention delivered by the Centre for Market and Public Organisation [CMPO], University of Bristol.)
report_number: EEF project: Teacher Observation (NFER evaluation, November 2017)
design: Cluster RCT (assignment = School; school-randomised efficacy trial). 82 secondary schools analysed (41 intervention / 41 control), high-FSM schools in England. Whole-school TPD intervention: teachers in maths and English departments trained (lead teachers cascaded) to use RANDA TOWER software on tablet computers to conduct structured 20-minute peer classroom observations over two years -> classified by the meta-analysis as 'TPD for digital tools', 'Long' duration, single arm vs business-as-usual control. Primary cohort = Cohort 2 (Year 10 in 2014/15) with two years of exposure; primary outcome = combined GCSE English+maths point score in 2016. Grade band 7-12 (secondary; outcomes at end of KS4 / GCSE for Year 11).
problems: The report's Table 13 column is explicitly labelled 'Hedges g', so the reported standardised mean differences are already Hedges' g; no further J small-sample correction was applied by me. Impact SEs are not printed; I derived g_se from the reported 95% CIs (SE = CI width / (2 * 1.959964)) and g_var = g_se^2. These are EEF cluster-randomised, pretest-adjusted (KS2 prior attainment + stratifiers) multilevel-model effect sizes, so cluster_adjusted=true. ICC=0.046 is the school-level analysis-stage design ICC from Table 7 (power table), not a per-outcome observed ICC. n_t/n_c recorded are the per-outcome 'n in model' (intervention; control) from Table 13; n_t (missing) etc. raw-sample counts also noted. The headline primary outcome is a COMPOSITE (combined GCSE English+maths) that mixes Reading and STEM; per spec it is recorded with outcome_subject=Other and role=composite, with the disaggregated GCSE English (Reading) and GCSE maths (STEM) recorded as its subscales. Only the school-level experiment (Table 13) is a TPD-vs-business-as-usual contrast; the department-level (Table 14, high vs low dosage) and teacher-level (Table 15/16, observer vs observed) experiments are WITHIN-intervention dosage/role comparisons (no business-as-usual control) and are therefore NOT extracted. Cohort 1 (2015 GCSE, only ~one year of exposure / Year 11 in 2014/15) and the interim Year 10 reading/maths tests are earlier/non-end-of-treatment waves and are noted but not extracted; the end-of-treatment full-exposure wave is Cohort 2's 2016 GCSE. Overall trial found no impact (g approx 0).

effect_sizes.test_name: GCSE English + maths combined point score (Cohort 2, 2016) - primary outcome
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (2016 GCSE; end of two-year intervention, Cohort 2 / Year 11)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported directly as Hedges' g in Table 13 (column 'Hedges g'): EEF cluster-randomised, KS2-prior-attainment-adjusted multilevel-model standardised mean difference. Taken as g unchanged. g_se = (0.06-(-0.08))/(2*1.959964) from reported 95% CI; g_var = g_se^2. Raw means 76.7 (95% CI 76.2,77.2) vs 76.1 (75.6,76.6); SDs not reported (model-based SMD).
effect_sizes.page_ref: p.31 Table 13 (School-level experiment impact analysis), row 'Primary Outcome: Cohort 2, 2016 GCSE English + maths'
effect_sizes.notes: Headline/primary confirmatory outcome. Composite combining GCSE English (Reading) + maths (STEM); recorded as Other per spec since it mixes subjects. n in model = 12,826 (6,827 int; 5,999 ctrl); raw post-test n = 7,366 (141 missing) int / 6,503 (153 missing) ctrl. p=0.802, not significant. MDES at analysis = 0.11. Equivalent to 0 months' additional progress.
